newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 27.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 27.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

CANNES - China is expected to become the world's fourth largest advertising market in the next five years and Western-based ad agencies foresee no problems with the Hong Kong handover, Miles Young, the head of Ogilvy & Mather's Asia-Pacific region, tells Reuters at International Advertising Festival in Cannes. The world's five biggest advertising markets at present are the U.S., Japan, Germany, France and Britain.
BRUSSELS - The European Union agrees on new legislation to prevent advertisers unfairly comparing their products to those of competitors.

CANNES - Martin Sorrell, chairman of WPP, the world's largest advertising and marketing services group, criticises advertising agencies for losing media-planning and media-buying business to media independents.
CANNES - Maurice Levy, the chairman of Publicis, says he's unhappy to learn from press reports of talks between U.S. advertising groups Bozell and True North Communications Inc of a possible link-up.
PARIS - Advertising in French men's magazines jump 36.4 percent in the first four months of 1997 compared with the same period in 1996, says magazine Carat Medias Actualites.
APELDOORN, Netherlands - Dutch publisher Wegener NV says it is in talks with the Sopres Group in Brussels on acquiring a 45 percent stake in direct marketing firm Sopres.
LOS ANGELES - BBDO West, part of Omnicom, resigns from the Apple Computer Inc advertising account after being told the account is coming up for review.
NEW YORK - Doremus Advertising, a unit of Omnicom Group Inc, wins the U.S. account for newspaper The Financial Times. The account is valued at between $3 million and $6 million.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
SAN FRANCISCO - President Clinton will announce a nine-point plan next week to spur electronic commerce around the world by making the Internet a tax-free zone, officials say.
BRUSSELS - The European Commission tells Belgium to scrap an advertising monopoly granted to Flemish commercial TV channel VTM.

LONDON - The British Soccer Premier League is set to demand more money from British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc for television rights next year when digital TV is launched, the London Evening Standard newspaper reports.
BRUSSELS - The European Commission opens legal proceedings against Spain, saying a law it adopted on decoders for digital and pay-TV services could restrict free trade.

KUALA LUMPUR - Despite the glut of cyberspace-related products, the economic success of the Internet remains unproven, and many businesses have failed to make it profitable, a U.S. software executive at Novell Inc says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - Burger King, the fast-food chain, says it is awaiting a "tangible upturn in consumer confidence" before it will buy British beef. "There are still a number of our customers who have concerns," a company spokeswoman says.

LONDON - Britain's government proposes an extension to the existing rights of landlords of "tied" pubs to offer their customers guest beers. Under present rules, one guest cask-conditioned, or "real" ale can be offered in every pub owned by a brewery. The change will mean tenants can offer a beer produced by another brewer as well.

PURCHASE, New York - PepsiCo Inc names its $10 billion restaurant company Tricon Global Restaurants Inc. Tricon, comprised of the global businesses of Pizza Hut, KFC and Taco Bell, will be spun off later this year.
HONG KONG - A new law in Hong Kong provides stronger legislative tools to combat piracy of branded consumer goods, a government spokesman says.
LONDON - A new enzyme product that bleaches the water instead of the clothes in the washing machine could make pink underwear a thing of the past, New Scientist magazine reports.

MOSCOW - Hundreds of thousands of bottles of fake branded vodka seized by Moscow police go to a chemical factory for re-processing into brake fluid and car windscreen cleanser, Interfax news agency says.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
GENEVA - Americans have hit the French where it really hurts -- they have criticised French cheese. America has angered the European Union by demanding the pasteurisation of imported dairy products.
BOMBAY - Executives at one of India's largest engineering firms have formed a laughter club which meets every day to laugh for 15 minutes and beat stress.

OTTAWA - The Supreme Court rules that the erotic practice of lap dancing is too indecent for Canada. Lap dancing, where bare-bottomed women gyrate on customers' laps, has become popular in strip joints across Canada but will now be banned.

NEW YORK - Most adult Americans have negative views of teenagers and children and believe the country's youth face a moral crisis, according to a study published by research organisation, Public Agenda. Two-thirds of Americans described teenagers as "rude," "irresponsible" and "wild.
